text:
### Observed differences

- In the later window, five activities that were previously absent or nearly absent run exactly once in every trace: A30, A31 and A32 were in 0 of 200 traces earlier and A20 and A21 in 1 of 200 each; later all five appear in 200 of 200 traces, with about one occurrence per trace [OCC005, OCC006, OCC011, OCC012, OCC013].
- A former group of optional tail activities has disappeared: A19, A23, A24 and A25, earlier in about 14–27 in 100 traces (28–54 of 200), are not observed at all later, and A22 fell from 50 to 2 of 200 traces. Earlier, each of them led back to A33 in about 91–96 in 100 of its outgoing transitions, and they largely excluded one another within a trace; those edges are no longer observed [OCC004, OCC007, OCC008, OCC009, OCC010, DIR003, DIR006, DIR007, DIR008, DIR009, REL047, REL057].
- A04 became far more prominent: from about 10 in 100 traces (mean 0.11 occurrences per trace) to about 73 in 100 traces (mean 0.79), and it now appears earlier and much more consistently within traces (median position about 0.38 → 0.30; 75th percentile about 0.88 → 0.33) [OCC001, POS001].
- Routing around A48 changed: earlier its outgoing transitions went mostly to the tail activities (A23 about 25 in 100, A22 about 20, A25 about 16, A19 about 15, A24 about 13); later about 70 in 100 go to A04, whose outgoing transitions in turn go about 87 in 100 into the new block (A20 about 22, A32 about 20, A31, A21 and A30 about 15 each). In about 99 in 100 later observations A48 is immediately followed by A04, though the earlier profile rests on only 4 observations [DIR013, DIR001, LAG001].
- The new block sits between A48/A04 and A33: A48 precedes each block activity in at least about 98 in 100 traces, A04 precedes them in about 64–65 in 100, and each block activity precedes A33 in about 97–99 in 100 traces. Within the block there is no fixed order (for example A20 precedes A21 in about 52 in 100 traces and A21 precedes A20 in about 47) [REL012, REL033, REL044, REL076, REL081, REL085, REL002, REL003, REL008, REL009, REL010, REL032, REL043, REL075, REL080, REL084, REL024, REL073, REL079].
- A33 now occurs later in traces (mean position about 0.39 → 0.48) and A48 slightly earlier (about 0.33 → 0.28), consistent with a block of activities being inserted between them; A04 also now co-occurs with A33, A48, A53 and A54 in about 73 in 100 traces, where earlier it co-occurred with each in only about 10 in 100 [POS012, POS013, REL011, REL012, REL013, REL014].

### Inference

Support level: Supported hypothesis

The evidence supports the hypothesis of a structural replacement in the later part of the process: the former optional tail, in which typically one of A19, A22, A23, A24 or A25 executed after A48 and led back to A33, is no longer observed, and in the later window a new group of five activities — A20, A21, A30, A31 and A32 — executes once in every trace between A48 and A33, usually mediated by A04 (A48 → A04 in about 70 in 100 of A48's outgoing transitions, then A04 into the block). The block's members follow A48 and precede A33 in stable order but are mutually unordered [OCC004, OCC007, OCC008, OCC009, OCC010, OCC005, OCC006, OCC011, OCC012, OCC013, DIR013, DIR001, DIR003, DIR006, DIR007, DIR008, DIR009, REL033, REL032, REL024].

The signs are direct and consistent across indicator families: participation moves from 0–1 of 200 traces to 200 of 200 and from 28–54 of 200 to 0–2 of 200; the successor profiles of A48 and A04 change on the same traces; the relation items show the new block co-occurring with A48, A04 and A33 in stable orders while its members are interchangeable in order; and the position shifts of A33 and A48 fit an inserted segment. Screening produced 130 qualifying items against about 1 expected if nothing had changed, so sampling variation in these windows cannot account for the pattern as a whole [DIR013, DIR001, POS012, POS013, OCC005, OCC011, OCC008, REL032, REL024].

An important competing explanation remains: the evidence cannot rule out that A20, A21, A30, A31 and A32 are relabelled versions of A19, A22, A23, A24 and A25 rather than genuinely new activities, since anonymous labels cannot be matched across windows; what the evidence shows is the substitution of behaviour, not activity identity. Also, A04 is absent in about 27 in 100 later traces, where A48 appears to lead directly into the new block, so mediation by A04 is typical but not universal [OCC005, OCC011, DIR013, OCC001].

Other differences: A08 and A10 occur less often (about 18 → 7 and 19 → 8 in 100 traces), and A10's successor mix changed, though only 17 outgoing transitions support its later profile; A22's two residual occurrences led to A09 and A14 instead of A33 (based on 2 traces, weak). The A53 → A54 pair became slightly more tightly adjacent (immediately-following share about 87 → 97 in 100) [OCC002, OCC003, DIR002, DIR006, LAG002].
